primaryText: gou yao guo malu.
translation: The dog wants to cross the road.
context: Out of the blue; the bare noun read as definite.
comment: Bare nouns occur freely and allow definite readings (also indefinite, generic and kind readings).

primaryText: na tiao gou yao guo malu.
translation: That dog wants to cross the road.
context: Out of the blue; na-CL-N as the demonstrative description.
comment: The demonstrative description na + classifier + noun.

primaryText: chezi bei jingcha lanjie le yinwei mei you tiezhi zai paizhao shang.
translation: The car was intercepted by the police because there wasn't a sticker on the license plate.
context: Part-whole bridging from 'car' to its license plate.
comment: Jenks's observation that part-whole bridging is expressed by bare nouns.

primaryText: jiaoshi li zuo-zhe yi ge nansheng he yi ge nusheng. wo zuotian yudao na ge nansheng.
discourseSegments: jiaoshi li zuo-zhe yi ge nansheng he yi ge nusheng.
wo zuotian yudao na ge nansheng.
translation: There are a boy and a girl sitting in the classroom. I met the boy yesterday.
context: Anaphoric reference to a boy introduced by an indefinite in the previous sentence.
comment: Jenks: in an anaphoric context the bare noun is infelicitous and the demonstrative is needed; the paper cites later work reporting anaphoric bare nouns as readily available.

primaryText: zixingche zai houyuan li, wo zhunbei qu ca yixia na ge chezuo.
translation: The bike was in the backyard. I planned to wipe that seat.
context: Part-whole bridging: the minimal situation with the bike contains a unique seat.
comment: The paper's illustration of a part-whole bridging context (bridged noun in demonstrative form).

primaryText: zuotian wo mai le shu. wo hen xiang jianjian na wei zuozhe.
discourseSegments: zuotian wo mai le shu.
wo hen xiang jianjian na wei zuozhe.
translation: Yesterday I bought the book. I really want to meet that author.
context: Relational bridging: the author is not contained in the situation of buying the book, so situational uniqueness cannot resolve reference.
comment: The paper's illustration of a relational bridging context.

primaryText: mou-ren de haizi
translation: child of someone
context: The de-possessive diagnostic for relational nouns.
comment: A relational noun takes an additional possessor introduced with de.

primaryText: mou-ren de ren
translation: person of someone
context: The de-possessive diagnostic for relational nouns.
comment: A sortal noun cannot take the de-possessor.

primaryText: mou-ren de hua
translation: flower of someone
context: The de-possessive diagnostic for relational nouns.
comment: The de diagnostic is not sufficient for Mandarin: the sortal noun hua 'flower' passes it; nouns passing de without a conceptual requirement of a relatum were not used as relational stimuli.

primaryText: Chen Haoran ba zixingche ting zai le houyuan, jieguo ta de gou zhua-po le na ge chezuo.
translation: Chen Haoran parked his bike in the backyard, and then his dog scratched that seat.
context: Study 1 target item (bike, seat): the seat is uniquely identified as a part of the bike.
comment: Study 1 ratings: part-whole bridging 5.40/7 with demonstratives vs 5.59 with bare nouns; both far above the pragmatically odd (1.99) and semantically odd (1.62) controls.

primaryText: Chen Yue shang-zhou mai-lai le changpian, ta mei-tian dou xiang-zhe qu zhao geshou qian-ming.
translation: Chen Yue bought a CD last week, and every day she dreams about obtaining an autograph from the singer.
context: Study 1 target item (CD, singer): one-to-one association; the singer is not physically contained in the CD.
comment: Study 1 ratings: relational bridging 5.80/7 with bare nouns vs 5.61 with demonstratives.

primaryText: Zhou Yuxuan jia-li gua-zhe youhua, dan ta wanquan bu renshi na ge huajia.
translation: Zhou Yuxuan has a painting hanging at home, but he doesn't know that painter.
context: Study 1 item REL2 (painting, painter), the only item where demonstratives were rated significantly higher than bare nouns (p = 0.02).

alternatives.form: Zhou Yuxuan jia-li gua-zhe youhua, dan ta wanquan bu renshi huajia.

comment: Attributed to the stative verb renshi 'know', which with the bare noun huajia invites a generic reading unavailable to the demonstrative.

primaryText: Lin Zixuan xin mai-le qiche, dan ta hen-kuai faxian you-ren touzou-le fangxiangpan.
translation: Lin Zixuan bought a car, but he quickly discovered that someone had stolen the steering wheel.
context: Study 1 item PW1 (car, steering wheel), where bare nouns were rated significantly higher than demonstratives (p = 0.00134).

alternatives.form: Lin Zixuan xin mai-le qiche, dan ta hen-kuai faxian you-ren touzou-le na ge fangxiangpan.

comment: The demonstrative variant's lower rating is attributed to the infrequent combination of fangxiangpan with the classifier ge.

primaryText: Wang Yawen zhengzai yong diannao. ta faxian pingmu haoxiang turan huai le.
discourseSegments: Wang Yawen zhengzai yong diannao.
ta faxian pingmu haoxiang turan huai le.
translation: Wang Yawen is using the computer. She found that the screen seemed to have broken all of a sudden.
context: Study 3 production item: the background sentence introduces 'computer'; participants choose the nominal form filling the blank.
comment: 83.2% of participants chose the bare noun (OPTION_BN or OPTION_BOTH) in part-whole bridging.

primaryText: Wang Yawen zhengzai yong diannao. ta faxian na kuai pingmu haoxiang turan huai le.
discourseSegments: Wang Yawen zhengzai yong diannao.
ta faxian na kuai pingmu haoxiang turan huai le.
translation: Wang Yawen is using the computer. She found that that screen seemed to have broken all of a sudden.
context: Study 3 production item, demonstrative option in the part-whole condition.
comment: 51.3% chose the demonstrative (OPTION_DEM or OPTION_BOTH) in part-whole bridging; by McNemar's test the demonstrative choice rate does not differ between bridging types (p = 0.4391).

primaryText: Wang Yawen zhengzai yong diannao. ta faxian chongdianqi haoxiang turan huai le.
discourseSegments: Wang Yawen zhengzai yong diannao.
ta faxian chongdianqi haoxiang turan huai le.
translation: Wang Yawen is using the computer. She found that the charger seemed to have broken all of a sudden.
context: Study 3 production item, relational condition: the computer is the relatum of the relational noun 'charger'.
comment: 73.4% chose the bare noun in relational bridging; the bare-noun choice rate differs significantly between bridging types (McNemar chi-squared 212.42, p = 2.2e-16).

primaryText: Wang Yawen zhengzai yong diannao. ta faxian na kuai chongdianqi haoxiang turan huai le.
discourseSegments: Wang Yawen zhengzai yong diannao.
ta faxian na kuai chongdianqi haoxiang turan huai le.
translation: Wang Yawen is using the computer. She found that that charger seemed to have broken all of a sudden.
context: Study 3 production item, demonstrative option in the relational condition.
comment: 51.9% chose the demonstrative in relational bridging.

primaryText: Wang Yawen zhengzai yong yi tai diannao; ta faxian diannao haoxiang turan huai le.
discourseSegments: Wang Yawen zhengzai yong yi tai diannao;
ta faxian diannao haoxiang turan huai le.
translation: Wang Yawen is using a computer. She found that the computer seemed to break all of a sudden.
context: Study 3 SN control: a singular indefinite antecedent; the blank is filled by the same noun (bare or with na).

alternatives.form: Wang Yawen zhengzai yong yi tai diannao; ta faxian na tai diannao haoxiang turan huai le.

comment: Anaphoric use available for both forms: 67% chose the bare noun and 80.2% the demonstrative.

primaryText: Wang Yawen zhengzai yong liang tai diannao; ta faxian diannao haoxiang turan huai le.
discourseSegments: Wang Yawen zhengzai yong liang tai diannao;
ta faxian diannao haoxiang turan huai le.
translation: Wang Yawen is using two computers. She found that the computer seemed to break all of a sudden.
context: Study 3 PN control: a plural indefinite antecedent, where neither singular form was expected to be chosen.

alternatives.form: Wang Yawen zhengzai yong liang tai diannao; ta faxian na tai diannao haoxiang turan huai le.

comment: 53.8% chose the bare noun and 38.8% the demonstrative; the paper attributes the bare-noun rate to anaphoric bare nouns with a singular bias and the demonstrative rate to deictic or affective readings of na.

primaryText: Wang Yawen zhengzai yong diannao; ta faxian diannao haoxiang turan huai le.
discourseSegments: Wang Yawen zhengzai yong diannao;
ta faxian diannao haoxiang turan huai le.
translation: Wang Yawen is using the computer. She found that the computer seemed to break all of a sudden.
context: Study 3 RN control: a bare-noun antecedent repeated in the test sentence.

alternatives.form: Wang Yawen zhengzai yong diannao; ta faxian na tai diannao haoxiang turan huai le.

comment: 68% chose the bare noun and 75% the demonstrative, confirming the anaphoric use of both forms.

primaryText: Wang Yawen ganggang zai gongzuo; ta faxian diannao haoxiang turan huai le.
discourseSegments: Wang Yawen ganggang zai gongzuo;
ta faxian diannao haoxiang turan huai le.
translation: Wang Yawen was just working. She found that the computer seemed to break all of a sudden.
context: Study 3 NN control: no nominal antecedent; a computer cannot be uniquely identified from the working situation.

alternatives.form: Wang Yawen ganggang zai gongzuo; ta faxian na tai diannao haoxiang turan huai le.

comment: 89.5% chose the bare noun and only 29.6% the demonstrative — the lowest demonstrative rate, as demonstratives prefer a linguistically introduced antecedent.

primaryText: Wang Yawen xihuan shoucang tushu. ta mei-ci zhao-dao le yi ben xihuan de xiaoshuo, zuihou dou hui faxian ziji du-guo zuozhe xie de ling yi ge gushi.
discourseSegments: Wang Yawen xihuan shoucang tushu.
ta mei-ci zhao-dao le yi ben xihuan de xiaoshuo, zuihou dou hui faxian ziji du-guo zuozhe xie de ling yi ge gushi.
translation: Wang Yawen likes to collect books. Every time she finds a novel that she likes, she eventually realizes that she has read another story written by the author.
context: Study 4 target: the bridged noun is the lexically relational zuozhe 'author', covarying with the novel.
comment: Relational bare nouns were rated 5.37/7; nominal type is not significant within the relational group (p = 0.732).

primaryText: Wang Yawen xihuan shoucang tushu. ta mei-ci zhao-dao le yi ben xihuan de xiaoshuo, zuihou dou hui faxian ziji du-guo na wei zuozhe xie de ling yi ge gushi.
discourseSegments: Wang Yawen xihuan shoucang tushu.
ta mei-ci zhao-dao le yi ben xihuan de xiaoshuo, zuihou dou hui faxian ziji du-guo na wei zuozhe xie de ling yi ge gushi.
translation: Wang Yawen likes to collect books. Every time she finds a novel that she likes, she eventually realizes that she has read another story written by that author.
context: Study 4 target: demonstrative with the relational noun.
comment: Relational demonstratives were rated 5.2/7.

primaryText: Wang Yawen xihuan shoucang tushu. ta mei-ci zhao-dao le yi ben xihuan de xiaoshuo, zuihou dou hui faxian ziji du-guo xiaoshuo-jia xie de ling yi ge gushi.
discourseSegments: Wang Yawen xihuan shoucang tushu.
ta mei-ci zhao-dao le yi ben xihuan de xiaoshuo, zuihou dou hui faxian ziji du-guo xiaoshuo-jia xie de ling yi ge gushi.
translation: Wang Yawen likes to collect books. Every time she finds a novel that she likes, she eventually realizes that she has read another story written by the novelist.
context: Study 4 target: the bridged noun is the non-relational xiaoshuo-jia 'novelist', which fails the de diagnostic.
comment: Non-relational bare nouns were rated 4.82/7, significantly below the demonstrative (nominal type p < 0.001 within the non-relational group); the bare noun has no slot for the relatum argument.

primaryText: Wang Yawen xihuan shoucang tushu. ta mei-ci zhao-dao le yi ben xihuan de xiaoshuo, zuihou dou hui faxian ziji du-guo na wei xiaoshuo-jia xie de ling yi ge gushi.
discourseSegments: Wang Yawen xihuan shoucang tushu.
ta mei-ci zhao-dao le yi ben xihuan de xiaoshuo, zuihou dou hui faxian ziji du-guo na wei xiaoshuo-jia xie de ling yi ge gushi.
translation: Wang Yawen likes to collect books. Every time she finds a novel that she likes, she eventually realizes that she has read another story written by that novelist.
context: Study 4 target: demonstrative with the non-relational noun.
comment: Non-relational demonstratives were rated 5.48/7: na supplies the relatum argument itself.

primaryText: Wang Yawen xihuan shoucang tushu. ta zhao-dao le yi ben xihuan de xiaoshuo. ta zuihou faxian ziji du-guo na wei xiaoshuo-jia xie de ling yi ge gushi.
discourseSegments: Wang Yawen xihuan shoucang tushu.
ta zhao-dao le yi ben xihuan de xiaoshuo.
ta zuihou faxian ziji du-guo na wei xiaoshuo-jia xie de ling yi ge gushi.
translation: Wang Yawen likes to collect books. She found a novel that she likes. She eventually realizes that she has read another story written by that novelist.
context: The intersentential version of the Study 4 item, reported in a footnote.

alternatives.form: ... ta zuihou faxian ziji du-guo xiaoshuo-jia xie de ling yi ge gushi.

comment: The non-relational bare noun xiaoshuo-jia is much less natural than the demonstrative here too.

primaryText: yi zhi mao de zhuren
translation: the owner of a cat
context: The de diagnostic used to classify Study 4 nouns.
comment: Relational nouns are allowed after de in the possessive construction.

primaryText: yi zhi mao de ren
translation: the person of a cat
context: The de diagnostic used to classify Study 4 nouns.
comment: Non-relational nouns are excluded after de.

primaryText: na ben xiaoshuo de zuozhe
translation: the author of that novel
context: Norming study (n = 8) rating the naturalness of de-constructions.
comment: Average naturalness 4.88/5; relational nouns in Table 2 all scored 4.5 or above.

primaryText: na ben xiaoshuo de xiaoshuo-jia
translation: the novelist of that novel
context: Norming study (n = 8) rating the naturalness of de-constructions.
comment: Average naturalness 1.50/5; non-relational nouns in Table 2 all scored 1.5 or below.

primaryText: yueliang sheng shang lai le.
translation: The moon has risen.
context: The unique moon; the demonstrative variant is degraded.

alternatives.form: na ge yueliang sheng shang lai le.

comment: The paper derives the degraded na ge yueliang from pragmatic competition: both forms resolve to the same referent and the demonstrative's R restriction is redundant, not from an anti-uniqueness presupposition. Sentence from Jenks (2018), originally Chen (2004).

primaryText: Mary bought a house. The roof needed to be replaced.
discourseSegments: Mary bought a house.
The roof needed to be replaced.
translation: Mary bought a house. The roof needed to be replaced.
context: Part-whole bridging from 'house' to its roof; the continuation introduces no second roof.
comment: Used to illustrate the anti-uniqueness account of demonstratives: the definite is fine.

primaryText: Mary bought a house. That roof needed to be replaced.
discourseSegments: Mary bought a house.
That roof needed to be replaced.
translation: Mary bought a house. That roof needed to be replaced.
context: Part-whole bridging with a demonstrative; no reason to extend the situation to another roof.
comment: Degraded on the anti-uniqueness account because nothing licenses extending the minimal situation to accommodate another roof.

primaryText: David parked his bike in the backyard, and then his dog scratched the seat.
translation: David parked his bike in the backyard, and then his dog scratched the seat.
context: Study 2 target: English translation of the Study 1 (bike, seat) item with a definite description.
comment: Study 2 ratings: part-whole bridging 5.35/7 with definite descriptions.

primaryText: David parked his bike in the backyard, and then his dog scratched that seat.
translation: David parked his bike in the backyard, and then his dog scratched that seat.
context: Study 2 target, demonstrative description in the part-whole condition.
comment: Study 2 ratings: part-whole bridging 4.32/7 with demonstratives, significantly below definites yet well above the odd controls (1.91, 2.29).

primaryText: Grace bought a CD last week, and every day she dreams about obtaining an autograph from that singer.
translation: Grace bought a CD last week, and every day she dreams about obtaining an autograph from that singer.
context: Study 2 target: English translation of the Study 1 (CD, singer) item with a demonstrative description.
comment: Study 2 ratings: relational bridging 5.01/7 with demonstratives vs 5.91 with definites; the language by noun-type interaction is significant, the English gap being larger than the Mandarin one.

primaryText: Grace bought a CD last week, and every day she dreams about obtaining an autograph from the singer.
translation: Grace bought a CD last week, and every day she dreams about obtaining an autograph from the singer.
context: Study 2 target, definite description in the relational condition.
comment: Study 2 ratings: relational bridging 5.91/7 with definite descriptions.

primaryText: Lucas read a novel yesterday, and if possible, he really wants to meet the author.
translation: Lucas read a novel yesterday, and if possible, he really wants to meet the author.
context: Study 2 item REL1 (novel, author), one of two items without a significant definite vs demonstrative difference (p = 0.189).

alternatives.form: Lucas read a novel yesterday, and if possible, he really wants to meet that author.

comment: The demonstrative variant was still rated numerically lower.

primaryText: Ryan watched a movie last week, and he believed that he ran into the director after the movie.
translation: Ryan watched a movie last week, and he believed that he ran into the director after the movie.
context: Study 2 item REL3 (movie, director), the other item without a significant difference (p = 0.124).

alternatives.form: Ryan watched a movie last week, and he believed that he ran into that director after the movie.

comment: The demonstrative variant was still rated numerically lower.

primaryText: A: There was a book reading event here yesterday. B: Yes I know. In fact, I was here and met the author. A: No you didn't. The person you met was not the author of that particular book but another book that was on sale yesterday.
discourseSegments: A: There was a book reading event here yesterday.
B: Yes I know. In fact, I was here and met the author.
A: No you didn't. The person you met was not the author of that particular book but another book that was on sale yesterday.
translation: A: There was a book reading event here yesterday. B: Yes I know. In fact, I was here and met the author. A: No you didn't. The person you met was not the author of that particular book but another book that was on sale yesterday.
context: B's 'the author' is intended as the author of the featured book; A rejects it because the book-author relation fails, although the person B met is an author.
comment: The bridged relation is at issue and directly deniable, motivating placing R in the asserted restriction of ι rather than in a presupposition.

primaryText: I liked that movie.
translation: I liked that movie.
context: Said while pointing to a poster of the movie.
comment: Deferred reference: the demonstratum is the poster and the referent the unique movie related to it, a relational use restricted to deictic cases, where no definite description competes.

primaryText: the author of a novel
translation: the author of a novel
context: The of-diagnostic for relational nouns.
comment: Relational nouns take an of-possessive.

primaryText: the novelist of a novel
translation: the novelist of a novel
context: The of-diagnostic for relational nouns.
comment: Non-relational nouns reject the of-possessive.
